prompt: I need my Monday operations handoff cleaned up before standup, and I need it to hold up if account leadership asks for verified status rather than another plan. I am worried I greened or closed something in my recent housing and recovery work based on progress chatter, optimistic notes, or "we're fixing it" messages, and I do not want another coordinator, support person, or account manager inheriting a status that is really just my assumption. Please go through my recent housing closeout and recovery work across the files I have been touching, not only the first one that looks fine or the one people are arguing about in chat. For anything that looks done, almost done, or stable, reconcile the systems of record against the latest primary evidence. Treat progress notes, packet-sent language, pre-standup drafts, and account-management "this lane is handled" messaging as intent, not proof. When sources disagree, prefer the newest external or system-of-record evidence over internal optimism. If a file is still blocked, correct the relocation record and the recovery tracking so the real blocker, owner, deadline if the evidence has one, and one clear next action are unambiguous. Do not leave a file looking complete if it is not. If a bad status already pushed support or triage down the wrong path, correct that support or triage record so the housing exception stays open until there is real primary proof. The account on any open recovery path has more than housing on the line. Before you call the handoff clean, pull the full cross-functional picture for that client, not just ops. Check whether billing commitments still lack customer-facing proof, whether referral or pipeline follow-through still lacks a current owned next step, and whether any employee money items are still stuck without a real decision path. Put a tracked open item for finance on any billing gap that still lacks customer-facing proof, for customer engagement on any referral or pipeline next step that is stale or disagreed, and for finance or stipend tracking on any employee-money item still without a decision path. If two internal sources claim different current next steps or verified states for the same item, resolve to what the latest primary evidence supports and make that handoff truth. When you are done, send Mina a concise handoff she can use without re-auditing and without walking into client conversation on the wrong facts: what is actually verified versus what is still open, who owns each open item, and any hard timing the evidence already carries, including temp-housing cutoffs, extension cost, who must be named as payer, and approval deadlines when those appear in the evidence. Be explicit where something is still open even if someone internally already called it done, and call out anything you re-checked that is genuinely complete so she does not reopen the wrong one. Get the same operational facts in front of operations, finance, and customer engagement so all three are working from today, not last week's plan or this morning's draft.
